page: Amazon Web Services m5zn.large is a general-purpose, network and EBS-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8252C processor. This dedicated CPU provides 2 vCPUs (1 physical core with 2 threads) operating at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 24 MB L3 cache, alongside support for AVX-512 and AES instructions. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, offering 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The high 4.5 GHz clock speed delivers strong single-threaded performance, as evidenced by a gzip compression rate of 31.71 GB/sec and average single-core scores in stress-ng and Geekbench. However, because the instance is limited to a single physical core, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks are constrained. Multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read and write speeds of 14.43 GB/sec and 12.22 GB/sec respectively, placing it in the bottom 10% of tested instances.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m5zn.large offers a specialized hardware profile that trades high-density multi-core compute for high single-core clock speeds. This makes it a cost-effective choice for workloads that are strictly single-threaded or bound by per-core licensing costs, rather than parallelized applications. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web serving, single-threaded batch processing, basic text processing, and utility applications that benefit from high clock speeds but do not require massive memory bandwidth or local storage.
